lines.text: Abner's men and Joab's men met at the pool of Gibeon, and twelve young men from each side were counted off.
The young men all fell together, and Abner and the men of Israel were defeated by David's servants.
Asahel chased Abner and refused to turn away, so Abner struck him with the butt of his sword and he died.
Joab blew the ram's horn and the troops stopped, and Asahel was buried in his father's tomb in Jericho.
The war dragged on, David grew stronger, and six sons were born to him in Hebron.
